description: The Northern Ireland Demand Flexibility Map is an interactive web map that helps system planners develop a flexibility strategy and implementation pathway for Northern Ireland. It was published by Osaru Agbonaye, Patrick Keatley, Ye Huang, Oluwasola Ademulegun and Neil Hewitt, with a Zenodo record first issued in December 2020 and updated to version 1.2 in July 2024, and its method is set out in the 2021 Applied Energy paper "Mapping demand flexibility: A spatio-temporal assessment of flexibility needs, opportunities and response potential". The map gives a spatio-temporal assessment of demand flexibility needs, opportunities, response potentials and system adequacy, with priority maps for planning. It has 14 map layers with over 120 sub-layers, filtering tools and satellite, terrain and street views. Coverage is Northern Ireland. The map is accessible in a browser at no cost, and the Zenodo record holds a PDF description under CC BY-NC 4.0. Caveats: the layers are viewed online, not offered as a download, and commercial reuse is not allowed. Simulation uses are siting storage, renewable generation or district heating and forecasting low carbon technology uptake by neighbourhood. Related records: data-cso-ireland-networked-gas-consumption covers energy demand in the Republic of Ireland.
